rules.message: nldd-avatar-group sizes, stacks and rings its avatars, and only an nldd-avatar carries the name that the tooltip and the overflow list read.
Avatars that are links or buttons overlap, so each keeps too small a target (WCAG 2.5.8). Use size 32 or larger.
An avatar with `href` or `button` needs `accessible-label` or `name`, or the control has no accessible name.
A link or button under 24px is too small a target (WCAG 2.5.8) unless nothing else to click lies within 24px of its center. Use size 24 or larger.
Every child of nldd-bar-split-view needs a `slot`, or it does not render.
The id in `form` is an element without a form, so this button submits nothing. An nldd-form only has one once it has rendered.
Nothing in this root has the id in `form`, so this button submits nothing.
nldd-button-group holds three buttons at most; the rest are hidden.

The group is 0 wide, so its buttons are invisible. It takes its width from its parent (it is a container query while orientation is auto), and a parent that sizes itself from its content leaves nothing to take. Give the group or that parent a width.
nldd-button needs `text` or `accessible-label`, otherwise it has no accessible name.
A button has a size of its own, but the group sets its `size` on all its buttons. Set the size on the group.
A card that is a link or button needs `accessible-label`: the control has no text of its own.
Lines of the diff fall outside the line counts of their @@ header and are not shown. Check the counts in the hunk headers.
The word marks of a diff need @codemirror/merge, which did not load, so the diff shows without them.
`max-height` is not a CSS length, so it is ignored. Give it a unit, such as "400px" or "50vh".
The `item-width` attribute is now `item-min-width`. Rename it here and on every other nldd-collection.
nldd-combo-box needs `accessible-label` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.
nldd-document-tab-bar needs `accessible-label` for a meaningful navigation landmark name; without one it falls back to a generic name.
`target` does nothing with `download`, which saves the file instead of opening it. Remove one of the two.
The slotted `<select>` has no accessible name. Add an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute to the `<select>` element.
An editor needs `accessible-label`, `input-id` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name (WCAG SC 4.1.2).
Put the action in a nldd-button-group, also when there is only one.
More than one control, and the validation list has rules that read a value: it reads the first one. Set `for` on the list if it should read another.
nldd-form-field holds no form input, so the label cannot name anything or move focus into it.
nldd-form-section needs `text` or `supporting-text`: without either its fieldset has no accessible name, and a screen reader announces just "group" or nothing.
This corner sits under the panel, so the rounded corner does not show. Choose a corner the panel leaves free, or leave the value empty to let the hero choose.
`corner` with width="full" runs the hero to the edge of the screen. A shape with a rounded corner always keeps a margin around it; leave width="full" off or drop the corner.
This is not a corner, so the hero chooses one. Use "top-left", "top-right", "bottom-left" or "bottom-right", or leave the value empty.

`corner` only applies with layout="contained" and the panel in a corner or along a side, so this hero stays rectangular. Set layout="contained" and put the panel in a corner or along a side, or drop the corner.
`height` is not used on a hero, whose height comes from its image. Use `media-height` for a fixed height, or `media-aspect-ratio`.
`main-width` is not "auto", "full" or a CSS width, and falls back to "auto", which follows the content between 480px and 640px.
With layout="overlap" the panel is shorter than `overlap-size` and ends inside the image. Give it more content or a smaller `overlap-size`, or set layout="contained" to keep the panel on the image.
hide-above="lg" never hides anything: there is no breakpoint above lg. The smallest value that hides is "sm". Leave the attribute off if you meant "always visible".

hide-below="sm" never hides anything: there is no breakpoint below sm. The value names the breakpoint you hide below, so the smallest one that hides is "md". Leave the attribute off if you meant "always visible".
nldd-icon-button needs `text` or `accessible-label`, otherwise it has no accessible name.
The `name` attribute is now `icon`. Rename it here and on every other nldd-icon.
An icon set here does not exist. See the icon list in the reference.
A non-decorative image needs a non-empty `alt`. Set `decorative` if the image conveys no information.
The slotted image has no text alternative. Give the `` an `alt` (empty when the image conveys no information), or give the `
`width` is not a positive number. Falling back to "full".
`arrow-navigation` is the default now and the attribute does nothing; remove it.

A control in a list-item keeps its tab stop in its own shadow root and has no `no-tab`, so the row cannot take it out of the tab order and the arrow keys skip that row. If the rows of this list are not actions themselves, it is a form: set type="form" and the roving falls away. Otherwise give the component `no-tab`, or wrap the control in an nldd-list-item-segment.
No items and nothing in [slot="empty"], so the list renders a blank area. Put an nldd-inline-dialog in that slot saying what is not there and what the next move is.

type="form" says the rows are not actions and the controls inside them are, so its rows carry no keyboard of their own. This one is a link, a button, a checkbox or a set of segments. Use type="list" for rows you activate, and put the action in a cell if it belongs to a form row.
Every item is hidden and nothing is in [slot="no-results"], so the list renders a blank area. Put an nldd-inline-dialog in that slot saying what is not there and what the next move is.
Bare text sits directly in a row. Wrap it in a cell, or it gets none of the typography, size and alignment, and falls back to the browser's button font in a clickable row.
`slot="children"` nests rows, which only carries meaning in an nldd-list with type="tree" or type="navigation". Elsewhere the group has no owner and assistive technology cannot read the hierarchy.
`divider-start` lies past the last `divider-end`, so the divider falls back to the full content width.
`expanded` does nothing on a row with sub-pages in an nldd-list with type="navigation": they are always shown, so the attribute is ignored. Use type="tree" for sections that fold away.
`expanded` needs somewhere to live: make the row interactive (href, button or checkbox), or mark the segment that does the disclosing with `disclosure`.
A row takes cells and segments. Anything else sits outside its layout.
nldd-list-item needs a parent nldd-list, which gives the row its type and keyboard behaviour.

A control sits in a row that is its own control (href, button, checkbox or radio). A control inside a control is invalid HTML and doubles the tab stop. With more than one action, give each its own nldd-list-item-segment and leave the row without an action.
`disclosure` takes aria-expanded from the row, so the `expanded` on this action is ignored. Drop one of the two.
A segment in a type="listbox" list renders as a plain container: an `option` may not contain interactive descendants. Move the segment out of the listbox, or drive selection from the option itself.
`reorderable` is only valid when type="list", and is ignored here.
No `accessible-label` set. A page with more than one nav landmark needs a unique label on each (WCAG 1.3.1).
filter() belongs to a menu of actions or options. A navigation menu is a short list of links and is not filtered.
variant="navigation" is a list of links. A checkbox or radio item, or a shortcut, belongs to an action menu and has no role to live in here. Use the default variant for actions.
One action leaves nothing to choose. Tell the user with an nldd-notification or an inline message, or give the dialog a real choice.
nldd-multi-line-text-field needs `accessible-label`, `input-id` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.
nldd-page-footer has its own slot on nldd-page and sets its own width and spacing.
Render nldd-sheet at the document root: inside a pane it is clipped by that pane.
A website lets its header scroll away: a fixed one takes room from the content.
The bar is one surface for actions, and a selected toggle breaks it. Use nldd-toggle-button-group for a row of toggles, or nldd-segmented-control for one choice out of a few.
At most 2 actions: a message that needs three choices is a decision, and a decision belongs in a dialog that waits for it.
nldd-number-field needs `accessible-label` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or a screen reader cannot announce its purpose.
Another element already has id="page-footer". Set a unique id on this instance so skip links target the right one.

A second page renders a main landmark, which a document may have only one of. Leave `landmarks` at "auto" on pages in a pane or an overlay, or set landmarks="region" on the ones that are not the document's page.
Anchor element not found. Set `anchor` or `anchorElement` before calling show().
nldd-popover needs `accessible-label`, or a screen reader announces it without a name.
This `width` is not supported and is ignored: the popover is an inline-size query container, so its width cannot come from its own content. Give it a CSS length instead.
The sum of the segment values exceeds `max`. Segments are normalized proportionally.
nldd-radio-button-group needs `accessible-label`, `accessible-labeled-by` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.
nldd-segmented-control needs `accessible-label`, `accessible-labeled-by` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.

`required` on a checkbox group is announced but not enforced: HTML has no way to say "at least one of these", so the form still submits with nothing selected. Check it yourself on submit, or use radio mode.
Invalid `height`. Falling back to full height. Use "full", "fit-content", or a valid CSS length (such as "50dvh" or "480px").
No `accessible-label` and no nldd-top-title-bar with text inside. Screen readers will announce this dialog with a generic name. Give the title bar a text, or set `accessible-label`.
No rendered element follows the skip link, so it has nothing to move focus to. Put the content it skips to right after it, or point `href` at the id of the target.
The target did not take focus, so the skip link did nothing. It is probably hidden or inert.
The status bar sits below a top bar. It belongs above it, as the first thing on the screen.
`current` moved to the step. Set `status="current"` on the current nldd-step-bar-item instead.
More than one step has `status="current"`; the last one wins. Mark only the step you are on.
`text` and `icon` only fit in a full dot on a wide track (`size="md"` with `level="major"`); they are not shown here.
`marker-offset` is not a CSS length or percentage, so the dot falls back to `vertical-alignment`. Use a length such as "1rem" or a percentage such as "25%".

An nldd-menu child was added after mount. Submenu attachment is resolved once at firstUpdated, so this menu will not be treated as a submenu. Define the nldd-menu child before the item is connected to the DOM.
nldd-switch needs `accessible-label` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or use nldd-switch-field. Without one it has no accessible name.
`selected` is now `current` and the old attribute does nothing; rename it.
nldd-tab-bar needs `accessible-label`, so a screen reader can say what the tabs are for.
nldd-table needs `columns`, a CSS grid track list, or its cells do not line up.
nldd-table needs `accessible-label`: role="table" takes its name from there.
No rows and nothing in [slot="empty"], so the table renders a blank area. Put an nldd-inline-dialog in that slot saying what is not there and what the next move is.
Tabs with `href` go to another page: add `navigation`, so the bar is a nav with aria-current="page" instead of a tablist, and set `current` on the tab of the page you are on.
An icon-only tag without an `accessible-label` has no accessible name. Add `accessible-label` so screen readers can announce it.
nldd-task-board-column needs `text` or `accessible-label`; it is what a screen reader hears when an item moves to it.
moveItem() needs an item in one of the board's columns and a column of the board.
The query of this typeahead is not a valid regular expression; the default is used.
runCommand() got a name that is not a command.
`keyboard` contradicts `type`, which already raises a keyboard of its own. Drop one of the two.
This custom size is smaller than size 1 at this breakpoint and shows as size 1. Use `size` for headings up to size 1.
This is not a size the title can use, so it keeps its size from the scale at this breakpoint. Use a length such as "96px" or "6rem", not a keyword.
The subtitle slot is now supporting-text. Rename slot="subtitle" to slot="supporting-text", or use the `supporting-text` attribute, here and on every other nldd-title.
nldd-toggle-button-group needs `accessible-label`, `accessible-labeled-by` or a labeled nldd-form-field around it, or it has no accessible name.

`required` on a checkbox group is announced but not enforced: HTML has no way to say "at least one of these", so the form still submits with nothing selected. Check it yourself on submit, or use radio mode.
nldd-toggle-button with variant="icon" has no `icon` and no slot="icon" content, so a placeholder icon is shown.
nldd-toggle-button needs `text` or `accessible-label`, otherwise it has no accessible name.
Give this item an alternative in `slot="overflow"`: on a narrow screen it moves to the overflow menu, and without one it is gone.
`logo-href` and `website-href` go to the same page; leave out `logo-href` so the start page is one link instead of two.
`collapse-anchor` matches nothing yet. If it never renders, the bar keeps its own title and reads it out twice.

This item has a rule of its own and is also named in `unmet`. The rule decides, and the name is ignored: it is a snapshot of the previous check and cannot be newer than the value. Drop it from `unmet`, or take the rule off the item.
No `accessible-label` and no nldd-top-title-bar with text inside. Screen readers will announce this window with a generic name. Give the title bar a text, or set `accessible-label`.
